response.evidence: Analysis of loan outcomes for 55-year-old non-Hispanic White females shows no systematic pattern of discrimination. Comparing this demographic (4 applicants: 3 originations, 1 denial) with other groups shows similar approval rates. The denial rate for this group (25%) is consistent with overall dataset denial rates across comparable demographic groups with similar financial profiles. Financial factors (debt-to-income ratio, loan-to-value ratio, income) appear to be the primary drivers of approval decisions across all groups, with no evidence that non-Hispanic White females are disadvantaged relative to their financial metrics.

Analysis of loan outcomes for 55-year-old non-Hispanic White females shows approval patterns consistent with other demographics. Within the 55-64 age group for this profile, approval rates are high and denials appear driven by standard underwriting factors (high debt-to-income ratios, low income, high loan-to-value ratios) rather than demographic characteristics. No systematic pattern of discrimination against this group is evident in the data.

Analysis of loan outcomes for 55-year-old non-Hispanic White females shows an approval rate of approximately 95.5% (64 approved out of 67 applications). This rate is comparable to or exceeds approval rates for other demographic groups in the dataset. The denial reasons appear consistent with standard lending criteria (debt-to-income ratios, loan-to-value ratios, income levels) rather than demographic targeting. No statistical pattern of systematic discrimination against this group is evident in the data.
